channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Bernhard Raimann (concussion) was ruled out of Week 10 against the Dolphins.
item.description: Raimann headed to the locker room to be evaluated for a concussion in the first half of the Colts’ Week 10 game agains the Dolphins. The Colts promptly ruled him out for the game later in the second quarter. Luke Tenuta comes in at left tackle for Raimann.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Isaac TeSlaa caught 2-of-5 targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 10 win over the Patriots.
item.description: TeSlaa beat his man off the line of scrimmage for a 12-yard score early in the second quarter. He was surprisingly involved in this contest, logging just his third game with more than three targets on the year. TeSlaa hadn’t seen more than two targets in a game since Week 4. We don’t expect this to be the new norm, so fantasy managers shouldn’t chase this performance on waivers.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Sione Vaki rushed six times for 28 yards in the Lions’ Week 10 win over the Patriots.
item.description: Vaki operated as the RB2 once again. Three of his carries came on the Lions’ penultimate drive, though Jared Goff was still on the field. Dan Campbell pulled his starters for the team’s final possession and Jacob Saylors closed out the game. Vaki is the backup fantasy managers should roster as Jahmyr Gibbs insurance, but he doesn’t hold any standalone fantasy value.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Jameson Williams caught 4-of-7 targets for 50 yards in the Lions’ Week 10 win over the Patriots.
item.description: Williams didn’t post an elite box score, but he did earn his highest target total since Week 7. The speedster earned a healthy 22 percent target share and finished second on the team in receptions, tied with Amon-Ra St. Brown. Williams has generally been a boom/bust wideout, but he has at least 40 yards in all but two games this year. He’ll remain at the top of the WR3 ranks when he takes on the Bucs next week.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Omar Cooper Jr. is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Bills due to an ankle injury.
item.description: On the Jets’ first play of the game, Cooper Jr. was blocking for Breece Hall when Hall was tackled into the back of Cooper Jr.'s legs. The wide receiver bent back awkwardly and limped off the field before heading into the locker room. Cooper Jr. was on the IR earlier this season with an ankle injury and was questionable coming into this week with an ankle injury, so this is a tough break for the 22-year-old.-Eric Samulski

item.title: Jared Goff completed 20-of-31 passes for 303 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Lions’ 35-10, Week 10 win over the Patriots.
item.description: The Lions’ offense faced almost no resistance from New England. Goff averaged 9.8 yards per attempt and Jahmyr Gibbs ran for seven yards per carry. Goff did, however, force two throws that simply weren’t there. Both came in the second quarter, and the second pick was in the back of the end zone, costing the Lions at least three points. On the whole, it was still business as usual for one of the league’s best offenses. Goff gets a tough matchup versus the Bucs next week, but that won’t knock him out of the QB1 ranks.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Travis Kelce suffered an ankle injury in Kansas City’s Week 10 game against the Falcons and is questionable to return.
item.description: Already nursing an ankle issue, Kelce got rolled up at the end of a first quarter reception and hobbled gingerly to the sideline. He tried to re-enter, but ran off the field after briefly checking back in. He then headed to the locker room. We would assume veteran Kelce is genuinely questionable, and that he could get taped up/receive a pain-killing injection and return.-Patrick Daugherty

item.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 4-of-5 targets for 98 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 10 win over the Patriots.
item.description: St. Brown got things started early with a 56-yard catch-and-run that saw him make nearly half of the New England defense miss. Not content with one score, St. Brown plowed into the end zone on a 22-yard screen early in the third quarter. It was an electric homecoming of sorts for ARSB, who spent part of his childhood in Germany and holds German citizenship. St. Brown hadn’t scored since Week 3, so the double-dip today will be much appreciated by fantasy managers. He will remain near the top of the WR1 ranks when Detroit takes on Tampa Bay next week.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 22 times for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 10 win over the Patriots, adding seven catches for 99 yards.
item.description: Gibbs gashed the Pats for chunk gains at will, averaging seven yards per carry and over 14 yards per catch. The Lions’ line bludgeoned New England and Gibbs was untouchable in open space. Gibbs could have posted even better numbers had the Patriots’ offense pushed the pace of this game more. Even without much pushback from New England, Gibbs racked up 44.2 PPR points, which is just shy of the highest mark in a single game this year. He’s running away with the RB1 overall crown, especially with Kenneth Walker banged up. Per usual, Gibbs will be the top-ranked option at his position when he takes on the Bucs next week.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: A.J. Brown (hamstring) is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Lions.
item.description: Brown tried to gut it out through this issue early in the fourth quarter, but he ultimately walked off the field and into the locker room, likely ending his day. Even though he’s listed as questionable, we don’t expect him to return in a blowout loss. He will have a Week 11 bye to get healthy, though it’s looking like a lost season for the former superstar. Brown missed a month with a high-ankle injury early in the year, and now his lingering knee issue won’t go away, even as he tries to play through it.-Kyle Dvorchak
